name: Predict weather from clouds
blurb: Clouds, wind direction and pressure trend give you a usable 6 to 12 hour forecast without any instrument except your eyes — and it works when the phone signal does not.
gear: Optional: a barometer or a watch with one
steps: Learn the cloud types by height and shape first — the sequence they arrive in is the actual forecast.
Learn the warm-front sequence: cirrus, thickening to cirrostratus with a halo, then altostratus, then rain within 12 to 24 hours.
Learn the cold-front signature: towering cumulus, a sharp squall, heavy short rain, then rapid clearing and cooler air.
Learn to read the pressure trend — a fast drop means wind and rain coming, a steady rise means settled weather.
Learn what wind direction typically brings in your region, which is local knowledge you can only build by observing.
Keep a daily journal for a month: sky at morning, your forecast, and what actually happened.
tips: The rate of change matters more than the absolute reading. A fast-falling barometer is the strongest warning signal there is.
Local terrain overrides general rules. Mountains and coasts make their own weather.
proof: Your 12-hour forecasts, made from the sky alone, beat guessing over a month of records.
